title: Stelow Interface Breadboard
description: The structured map of a selected interface: the places the user can be, the affordances in each, and the wiring between them. This JSON is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for the interface's shape; the prose in selected-interface.md is its commentary. The rendered diagram is a view of this file, never a second decision state.

interfaceId.description: The id of the selected interface this breadboard maps (the proposal id, e.g. 'A').

selectedBy.description: Who resolved the interface pick. Mirrors the selected-interface.md receipt.

scopeCoverage.description: Which delivery slices this interface serves, against the recorded Scope Map version.

places.description: Places — bounded contexts of interaction. A Place is perceptual: it is where the user is, in terms of what they can do right now. The blocking test decides it: if the user cannot interact with what is behind, it is a different Place.

id.description: Place id. P1, P2, ... for places; P2.1 for a subplace inside P2.

system.description: Which system this place belongs to, when the interface spans more than one (e.g. 'frontend', 'backend').

mode.description: For a mode-based place, the mode name (e.g. 'Read Mode', 'Edit Mode'). A mode that transforms the whole screen is its own Place.

affordances.description: Everything the user or the code can act upon. UI affordances (U) are what the user sees and touches; code affordances (N) are the methods, subscriptions, and stores underneath; data stores (S) hold state that is read and written.

id.description: Affordance id. U for UI, N for code, S for data store.

name.description: The specific thing, named so it can be pointed at. For code affordances, the real method or property name — 'DATABASE' is not an affordance.

place.description: The place this affordance belongs to. Containment, not wiring.

component.description: Which component or service owns it.

control.description: What triggers it: click, type, call, observe, write, render.

wiresOut.description: Control flow — what this triggers. Navigation wires to a PLACE id, not to an affordance inside it.

returnsTo.description: Data flow — where this affordance's output goes. A display with nothing feeding it is a gap.

tentative.description: True when the affordance is speculative — it may not survive the next shaping cycle.
